subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
title: Zacchaeus the Tax Collector
overview: Luke 19:2-10 tells how Zacchaeus, a rich chief tax collector, climbed a tree to see Jesus. In this sub-strand you will retell that story, see how Zacchaeus changed, and learn to use money with integrity. You will also talk about why turning from sin matters if we want to be like Christ.

lessons.title: The story of Zacchaeus
objectives: Retell Luke 19:2-10 in the correct order.
Name the people and the main actions in the story.
lessons.intro: Crowds can hide a short person. Zacchaeus wanted to see Jesus so much that he ran ahead and climbed a tree. What happened next changed him.
lessons.notes:
The story is in Luke 19:2-10. Read it in turns so that every learner hears the words of the Bible.

### What the passage says
Zacchaeus was a chief tax collector, and he was wealthy. He wanted to see who Jesus was, but he was short and could not see over the crowd. He ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree.

When Jesus reached the place, He looked up and told Zacchaeus to come down at once, because Jesus must stay at his house that day. Zacchaeus came down at once and welcomed Him gladly.

The people who saw this began to mutter. They said that Jesus had gone to be the guest of a sinner.

Zacchaeus stood up and said that he would give half of his possessions to the poor. He also said that if he had cheated anybody, he would pay back four times the amount.

Jesus said that salvation had come to that house that day, and that Zacchaeus too was a son of Abraham. Then Jesus said that the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.

### Keeping the order
A good retelling follows this order: Zacchaeus the rich chief tax collector; the crowd and the tree; Jesus calling him by name; the welcome; the crowd's complaint; the promise about money; Jesus' words about salvation. Do not add events that the passage does not tell. Draw Zacchaeus in the tree and share the drawing with a partner so the picture matches the reading.

keyWords.meaning: a person who collected taxes for the government
a leading tax collector, as Luke 19:2 describes Zacchaeus
the kind of tree Zacchaeus climbed so he could see Jesus

activity.title: Read and retell Luke 19:2-10
steps: Close the Bible and retell the story in the correct order.
Draw and colour Zacchaeus on a tree.
Share the drawings with peers and check that they match the passage.

practice.question: What work did Zacchaeus do, and what does Luke 19:2 say about his wealth?
practice.answer: He was a chief tax collector, and he was wealthy.

practice.question: Why did Zacchaeus climb a sycamore tree?
practice.answer: He was short and could not see Jesus over the crowd.

practice.question: What did Jesus say to Zacchaeus in the tree?
practice.answer: He told him to come down at once, because Jesus must stay at his house that day.

summary: Zacchaeus was a rich chief tax collector who climbed a tree to see Jesus.
Jesus called him and went to his house.
Jesus said He came to seek and to save the lost.

lessons.title: How Zacchaeus changed
objectives: Recount how Zacchaeus changed his behaviour.
Discuss why it is important to repent in order to be like Christ.
lessons.intro: Meeting Jesus did not leave Zacchaeus the same. He made promises about his money and the people he may have cheated. That change is what repentance looks like.
lessons.notes:
Before Jesus called him, Zacchaeus was known as a sinner. The crowd said so when Jesus entered his house. Tax collectors in that time were often disliked because they could take more than they should. The passage itself shows Zacchaeus ready to put wrongs right.

### The change
Luke 19:8 records his new behaviour:

- He would give half of his possessions to the poor.
- If he had cheated anybody, he would pay back four times the amount.

He did not only feel sorry. He said what he would do. Jesus answered that salvation had come to that house. The Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost. Zacchaeus was one of the lost people Jesus came to save.

### Lessons from the story
- Jesus knows people by name and looks for the lost.
- No one is too disliked for Jesus to save.
- Repentance includes turning away from cheating.
- A saved person cares for the poor.
- Saying sorry is joined to putting things right.

### Why repent
To repent means to turn away from sin and turn to God. Christians want to be like Christ, who is honest, generous and merciful. If we keep a sin and will not turn, we are not following Him. Tell a friend one way to turn away from a bad habit: admit it, ask God for forgiveness, and do the right action instead. For Zacchaeus, the right action was giving to the poor and paying back four times what he had cheated.

Sing a song about Jesus Christ as the Saviour who seeks and saves the lost.

keyWords.meaning: to turn away from sin and turn to God
being saved by Jesus, as He said had come to Zacchaeus' house
Jesus, who came to seek and to save the lost

activity.title: Lessons and a conversation about change
steps: State three lessons learnt from the story of Zacchaeus.
Tell a friend how to turn away from bad behaviour.
Discuss why repenting matters if we want to be like Christ.
Sing a song about Jesus Christ as the Saviour.

practice.question: What two promises did Zacchaeus make in Luke 19:8?
practice.answer: He would give half of his possessions to the poor, and if he had cheated anyone he would pay back four times the amount.

practice.question: What did Jesus say had come to Zacchaeus' house?
Why is it important to repent?
practice.answer: So that we turn from sin and become like Christ, who saves the lost.

summary: Zacchaeus promised to give half of his possessions to the poor and to repay four times anyone he had cheated.
Jesus said salvation had come to his house.
Repentance means turning from sin so that we can be like Christ.

lessons.title: Integrity when using money
objectives: Explain integrity in the use of money.
List ways of using money wisely, following Zacchaeus' example.
lessons.intro: Money can be used to help or to cheat. Zacchaeus had become rich as a tax collector. After meeting Jesus, he chose honesty and generosity. That is integrity.
lessons.notes:
Integrity means being honest right through, even when nobody is checking. With money, integrity means you do not take what is not yours, you do not cheat in a price or a tax, and you do what you said you would do.

### What Zacchaeus teaches about money
He did not say, "I will enjoy my wealth and forget the people." He said half of his possessions would go to the poor. He said cheating would be repaid four times. Four times is more than giving back the same amount. It shows he wanted to repair the harm fully.

He also kept serving. The story does not say he ran away from his work. It shows him putting right the wrongs that work had made possible. A person can do a hard job and still be honest.

### Ways to use money wisely
- Keep money that is yours. Return money that you find or that belongs to a friend.
- Do not cheat a buyer or a seller.
- Share with someone in need, as Zacchaeus promised to share with the poor.
- Pay back anything you took wrongly.
- Do not waste school fees or money a parent gave you for a set purpose.
- Give thanks to God for what you have, whether it is little or much.
- Write down what you spend so you remember where it went.

A learner shows integrity by refusing to steal a coin from a desk and by sharing lunch without boasting. Jesus saves people so that their money habits change too. Pray and ask Him to make you honest with every coin you hold.

keyWords.meaning: honesty that stays the same even when nobody is watching

examples.problem: A shopkeeper's child is sent to buy bread and is given too much change. What would integrity look like?
steps: The extra money is not his.
Zacchaeus promised to pay back what was wrongly taken.
The child should return the extra change.
examples.answer: He should return the extra money to the shopkeeper.

activity.title: List wise ways to use money
steps: List ways of using money wisely.
Beside each way, say how it is like or unlike Zacchaeus after he met Jesus.
Role-play returning extra change and sharing with a classmate who has none.
Sing a song about Jesus the Saviour.

practice.question: What is integrity?
practice.answer: Being honest right through, even when nobody is watching.

practice.question: How did Zacchaeus show integrity with money?
practice.answer: He promised to give half of his possessions to the poor and to pay back four times anything he had cheated.

practice.question: Give two ways a learner can use money wisely.
practice.answer: Any two: return what is not yours, do not cheat, share with the needy, pay back what you took, do not waste money given for a set purpose.

summary: Integrity means honesty even when nobody is watching.
Zacchaeus gave to the poor and repaid cheating four times.
Use money to help, not to cheat.

quiz.question: Where is the story of Zacchaeus found?
Zacchaeus was a...
quiz.explanation: Luke 19:2 says he was a chief tax collector and wealthy.

quiz.question: Why did he climb a tree?
quiz.answer: He was short and could not see Jesus because of the crowd.

quiz.question: What did the crowd say when Jesus went to Zacchaeus' house?
options: They praised Zacchaeus for his honesty
They muttered that Jesus was the guest of a sinner
They asked Zacchaeus to be king
They climbed the tree with him
quiz.explanation: Luke 19:7 says the people muttered that Jesus had gone to be the guest of a sinner.

quiz.question: Zacchaeus said he would give how much of his possessions to the poor?
quiz.explanation: Luke 19:8 says he would give half of his possessions to the poor.

quiz.question: If Zacchaeus had cheated anyone, he promised to pay back:
quiz.explanation: Luke 19:8 says he would pay back four times the amount.

quiz.question: Jesus said the Son of Man came to...
Why is repentance important for someone who wants to be like Christ?
options: So they can keep cheating quietly
So they turn from sin and follow Christ's ways
So they can hide from Jesus
So they become richer by any means
quiz.explanation: Being like Christ means turning from sin, as Zacchaeus turned from cheating.

quiz.question: Integrity with money means...
options: taking extra change and keeping quiet
being honest even when nobody is watching
counting other people's money in secret
quiz.explanation: Integrity is honesty that does not depend on being watched.

quiz.question: Which action copies Zacchaeus' new behaviour?
options: Keeping a coin you found in a friend's desk
Returning what is not yours and sharing with someone in need
Cheating a younger child in a game of money
quiz.explanation: Zacchaeus repaid wrong and gave to the poor.
